Subject: Hosted API — duplicate response behavior — interim findings and mitigation

Hi all —

Summary (interim): our telemetry shows a small subset of requests routed through a newly deployed router change experienced a KV-cache race during suffix assembly, which, for very short prefix lengths, resulted in repeated assembly of the last output block. The behavior is deterministic given the execution trace we captured and explains the duplicated paragraphs. Impact window: 08:48:30–09:05:20 UTC. Approximate affected traffic: 3.6% p95 of requests in that window; error rate (incorrect inference output) ~0.4% of total tokens served.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the router change at 09:12 UTC to stop further incidence.
- Deployed a conservative guard in the KV cache path at 09:28 UTC to prevent the race condition (hotfix ID: RKF-1143).
- Enqueued a follow-up patch to harden assembly safety (target deploy: 2026-11-07T20:00:00Z UTC).

Customer-facing mitigation we recommend:
- Continue using Hosted API; duplication is currently mitigated by the rollback and guard.
- If you see duplicated output for an in-flight demo, you can drop duplicate contiguous blocks that match >95% token overlap as a temporary client-side filter.

Attachments: debug-log-20261107.txt (server traces sanitized)

We've opened internal incident INC-20261107-rc1 and published an interim note on the public status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20261107-rc1

Evelyn (on behalf of Runtime & Incident Ops)
VP, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
